author: phase1a-evidence-successor-lane
purpose: Define how each public contract evolves. Without this, a small contract set is a promise with no mechanism — and the one contract whose artifacts live in user repositories has no upgrade path.

decisionDependencies.claim: structure is governed by a small set of public versioned contracts, not a package count
the recipe is versioned independently of the fact schema; skipped releases must not mass-invalidate
consumers pin a schema major and receive a typed refusal rather than a reshaped document
physical storage schema is private and freely migratable
exit classes are a public contract with executable goldens
decisionDependencies.direction: VERSIONING depends on D9 for the additive-only exit-class rule (V4). D9 does NOT depend on VERSIONING.
decisionDependencies.note: B-SCV2-06: v1 cited D9 v1.4 while scope-correction v2 asserted D9 depends on VERSIONING, making ownership circular or hidden. The direction is now declared and VER-DEP checks the citation resolves to the live binding artifact.

decisionDependencies: evaluation-proof.v8.json (durable cold stored-read authority reconstruction; current candidate)
retention-tiers.v13.json (cold-reconstruction custody identity rejoin; current candidate)

principle.core: A contract's evolution policy is determined by WHO HOLDS ITS ARTIFACTS, not by how important it feels.
principle.rationale: If the artifacts live only in our release, a breaking change costs a version bump. If they live in user repositories, a breaking change costs every user a migration they did not ask for — and if it happens silently, it costs their trust in the gate. These are different problems and cannot share one policy.
principle.consequence: Contracts are classified by artifact custody, and the custody class dictates the mechanism.

custodyClasses.meaning: Artifacts are created by the tool and stored in the user's repository, under their version control, outliving any release.

policy.breakingChange: Requires a migrator, not a major bump alone.
policy.support: Last K majors readable, K >= 2, published as a number not a vibe.
policy.negotiation: Every artifact self-declares the version it was written under. The host reads the declaration; it never infers from shape.
policy.unsupportedVersion: INDETERMINATE with repair instructions. NEVER a silent re-interpretation and never a mass net-new diff.
policy.migration: Explicit, previewable, and idempotent. `--check` shows the diff without writing.
policy.dualEmit: Where two identities can be computed, emit both during the transition window so a mid-upgrade fleet matches on either.

custodyClasses.why: This is the class that can destroy trust. A user who skipped three releases and comes back to a flood of false net-new findings concludes the gate is unreliable — and they are right to.

custodyClasses.meaning: No stored artifact, but an external consumer's code depends on the shape at runtime — CI scripts, agents, dashboards.

policy.breakingChange: New major, offered alongside the old for a published window.
policy.negotiation: The consumer requests a major explicitly. An unsupported request is a typed refusal, never a best-effort reshape.
policy.additive: New optional fields are minor. A consumer that rejects unknown fields is non-conforming; this must be stated so additive change stays cheap.
policy.exitCodesSpecial: Exit classes may only be ADDED, never renumbered or repurposed. A build script cannot negotiate.

custodyClasses.why: The failure mode is silent: a reshaped document parses, produces a different meaning, and CI does the wrong thing without erroring.

custodyClasses.meaning: Third-party authors compile or validate against it.

policy.breakingChange: New major with an overlap window; contributions declare a supported range and the host refuses outside it at admission, not at first use.
policy.negotiation: Handshake at admission: host advertises supported ranges, contribution declares its requirement, mismatch is an admission rejection with both ranges named.
policy.deprecation: Announce, then warn on use, then refuse. Each stage is a release, not a day.

custodyClasses.why: Cheaper than user-custody because authors can respond to a release; more expensive than internal because they are not us.

custodyClasses.meaning: No external party depends on the shape.

policy.requirement: Anything derived must be REBUILDABLE from retained inputs, or it is not internal — it is evidence, and evidence is user-custody.
policy.test: If deleting it loses information a retained Run needs, it was misclassified.

custodyClasses.why: The whole point of keeping storage private is to be able to change it. If internal layouts acquire external dependents, that freedom is lost silently.

versionedIdentities.note: Not itself a contract; the vehicle.
Family distinguishes this contract from any predecessor with a colliding version number.
Independent of the fact schema — that independence is the whole reason it exists.
Relation-level granularity so adding a relation does not break rules that never used it.

versionedIdentities.retainedRunRule: A retained trusted declarative semantics object binds its exact IR major, verifier ABI, canonical semantics bytes and a bundled signed content-addressed verifier artifact. Current-host defaults never reinterpret it.
PolicySemanticsRef uses the same historical-verifier binding as PredicateSemanticsRef.

versionedIdentities.form: content-addressed bytes + exact verifier ABI + exact supported IR family/major + signed bundle provenance
versionedIdentities.why: Reachable from a retained verifiable/replayable Run, therefore USER-CUSTODY by V7. A new IR major requires a new artifact identity; an old Run keeps its old reference.
A1-VER-06. Reachable from a retained Run, therefore USER-CUSTODY by V7 whatever it was labelled.

rules.rule: Every public contract declares exactly one custody class. Unclassified means unshippable.
A USER-CUSTODY breaking change without a migrator is prohibited, regardless of how the version is numbered.
No consumer-facing document is reshaped in place. Either the consumer's requested major is served, or the request is refused with the supported range named.
Exit classes are additive-only, forever. Renumbering silently changes the meaning of every CI configuration in existence.
Compatibility is negotiated at admission, not discovered at first use. A contribution incompatible with the host fails to load with both ranges reported.
Support windows are published as concrete counts and dates. 'We support recent versions' is not a policy.
Anything reachable from a retained Run is USER-CUSTODY by definition, whatever it was labelled. Custody follows reachability, not intent.

A version identity that participates in PlanId cannot change without changing derived identity — so bumping it invalidates caches by construction. This is a feature; do not add compatibility shims that hide it.

Any change that makes a byte sequence reachable from a retained Run is a VERSIONING REVIEW EVENT. Reachability is checked mechanically: the evidence reachability graph must never point at a path the inventory labels INTERNAL.
rules.why: V7 says custody follows reachability, which means custody can change SILENTLY — a refactor that starts embedding an internal structure in a Run has just made it USER-CUSTODY without anyone deciding to. A1-VER-03.

rules.rule: For bundled trusted declarative v1 rule/policy semantics, PredicateSemanticsRef and PolicySemanticsRef bind exact canonical semantics bytes, IR family and major, verifier ABI, and a signed bundled content-addressed verifierArtifactRef. A verifiable or replayable closure retains or resolves that exact compatible offline artifact. A major change creates a new artifact; old Runs are immutable and never silently reinterpreted. Unavailable or unsupported semantics/verifier material becomes a typed unavailable capability dependency for retention-tiers.v7, or an authoritative read is refused through existing D9. Proof migration creates a new Run and never rewrites the old Run identity.
rules.scope: Only trusted bundled declarative v1 semantics. Untrusted imperative code and Probe are excluded.

fingerprintRecipe.note: Plus an explicit previewable upgrade path. Beyond the window: INDETERMINATE, never a reinterpretation.

historicalRulePolicySemantics.majorsSupported: artifact-custody-derived; no fixed count or date
historicalRulePolicySemantics.evidenceGrade: PROVISIONAL — exact support exists only while the content-addressed semantics, signature material and compatible offline verifier artifact remain resolvable

supportWindows.caveat: These numbers are chosen for coherence, not from adoption data. They are the most guessed part of this artifact and should be revisited when real usage exists (A19).
supportWindows.sealRule: No support window may be SEALED while its evidenceGrade is GUESSED without a recorded product disposition. VER-EG enforces this.
supportWindows.consumerFacingRule: Any consumer-facing support matrix MUST display evidenceGrade (or the word provisional) next to each window. GUESSED numbers must not be presented as SLAs (R1-VER-02). VER-EG continues to forbid sealing windows while GUESSED without product disposition.

conformanceTests.assert: Every public contract declares exactly one custody class; an unclassified contract fails the release gate.
A USER-CUSTODY breaking change without a SPECIFIED migrator is refused by the release gate.
conformanceTests.note: A1-VER-01: this was vacuous in v1 because no migrator existed for any member. Four are now specified; run-manifest is NOT-YET-ENFORCEABLE and is excluded from discharge.

conformanceTests.assert: A consumer requesting an unsupported major receives a typed refusal naming the supported range, never a reshaped document.
Exit classes can be added but never renumbered or repurposed.
A contribution incompatible with the host fails to load at admission with both ranges reported.
Every migrator runs offline from in-release code and fetches nothing.
`--check` previews a migration without writing, and running a migrator twice is a no-op.
A baseline comparison across a detector change classifies each difference as CODE-NET-NEW, DETECTION-DELTA, or CODE-FIXED using the detector pivot.
When the pivot detector is unavailable the comparison reports INDETERMINATE for it and never attributes the delta to code.
A waiver whose target identity changes under migration is reported individually, never summarised.
The evidence reachability graph never points at a path the inventory labels INTERNAL.

conformanceTests.requiresHarness: adoption telemetry that does not exist and that the threat model may forbid
conformanceTests.assert: Support windows match observed user upgrade behaviour.
conformanceTests.note: A1-VER-05: the numbers are GUESSED. Marking this unimplementable is the honest state — and note the harness may be unbuildable by design, since the threat model's zero-egress posture forbids the telemetry that would inform it.

conformanceTests.assert: Canonical semantics bytes exactly equal the selected signed manifest binding for payload ref, manifest ref, IR family/major, verifier ABI, and trust profile.
A current host on a newer IR major verifies an old Run with the old retained verifier artifact without changing the Run identity.
Missing/incompatible semantics, native payload, manifest, signature, trust root, public key, platform, target, executable ABI, entrypoint, or verifier ABI yields typed deterministic refusal.
Changing IR major requires a different verifierArtifactRef; the same artifact cannot silently span majors.
A proof migration emits a new Run identity with explicit lineage; rewriting the old Run is rejected.
Untrusted imperative semantics and Probe are outside the historical verifier policy.
Historical interpretation support is derived from artifact custody/capability, never a fixed support-window or cost/SLA promise.
Every verifier manifest signature verifies offline with retained raw Ed25519 public-key bytes under the pinned trust root; TOFU and network lookup are false.
Every manifest contains the exact complete DELIVERY v2 supported-platform set and a content-addressed native Rust payload per platform.
Historical selection is exact by platformId, targetTriple, executableAbi, mediaType and entrypoint; incompatible host identity refuses.
Manifest payload/family/major/ABI/key substitutions reject even when the substituted manifest has a valid test signature.
Semantics verifier ref or ABI disagreement with the selected binding rejects.
Executable bytes, public key or signature substitution rejects after exact CAS and cryptographic verification.
A JSON descriptor without native payload bytes cannot satisfy verifierArtifactRef.
The historical decision derives the exact six-object minimum-verifiable dependency set for the selected platform.

peerReviewRequired: Is the detector pivot affordable? It requires running the OLD detector over new code on every comparison that crosses a detector version — potentially doubling analysis cost during a transition window.
Blind re-authoring of the seven comparison fixtures.
A1-VER-05 needs a PRODUCT owner. Every support window is a guess and may stay one.
Blind re-author the historical semantics and cross-major fixtures; verify artifact-custody demotion/refusal without introducing a second capability lattice.
Independently re-author the native payload CAS, signed per-platform manifest, trust-root/key chain, RFC8032 verification, exact semantics equality, and all R12-EVD-01 controls.
knownLimitations: Every support window is GUESSED and the corresponding property is NOT DISCHARGED. VT-12's harness may be unbuildable by design.
The detector pivot doubles work during a transition window; no measurement supports the claim that this is affordable.
The run-manifest migrator is NOT-YET-ENFORCEABLE, so evidence bundles are USER-CUSTODY by V7 with no migration path.
Authored in the Evidence v3 repair lane; independent re-review remains required.
Historical rule/policy interpretation has no fixed support-window or cost promise. It depends on exact artifact custody and compatible offline verifier support.

Native verifier payload bytes, signatures and trust roots are deterministic design fixtures. The checker verifies custody and signatures but does not execute a payload or demonstrate product behavior.
Evidence v3 remains bound to VERSIONING v3 and frozen Phase1A v2/v7. A later Evidence version must explicitly rejoin VERSIONING v4 and independently accepted Phase1A v3/v8 bytes.
VERSIONING v5 is a candidate-only EP5/RT10 join. It is not product acceptance, implementation evidence, or permission to apply the candidate.
Evidence rejoin is downstream-owned; this artifact deliberately carries no Evidence artifact or checker hash in capabilityJoin.
VERSIONING v6 is a not-applied candidate and has no Evidence back-edge or product authority.
The raw authority lineage is mechanically specified but not executed or independently accepted.
VERSIONING v7 preserves v6 identity/custody values and only rebinds authority provenance to EP7/RT12.
No production store/transaction implementation or atomicity evidence exists; candidate remains not applied/unaccepted.
VERSIONING v8 preserves v7 historical-verifier custody and every semantic/versioned identity; it only rejoins current authority to EP8/RT13 cold stored-read reconstruction.
EP8/RT13 exercise an in-memory cold-open specification. They do not demonstrate a production restart, durable backend, transaction, recovery or atomicity implementation.
EP8/RT13 are the only current successor dependencies. Older EP/RT labels retained in protected predecessor material describe historical candidate lineage, not current inputs.

migrators.why: A1-VER-01: V2 forbids a USER-CUSTODY breaking change without a migrator, and v1 specified no migrator for any member. A prohibition with no named mechanism is vacuous, and it was discharging a sealed property.

airGap.rule: A migrator SHIPS IN THE RELEASE. It may not fetch anything.
airGap.consequence: If a transition genuinely needs data not present locally, it is NOT a migrator — it is a re-analysis, and it must be reported as such rather than disguised as an upgrade.
airGap.why: The air-gap posture and the migrator obligation collide the moment a migrator needs the network. Resolving it in favour of in-release packaging keeps both promises; resolving it the other way would quietly break air-gap for exactly the users who care most.

members.preview: --check prints the full identity diff and writes nothing
members.witness: the recipe version declared in the baseline file
the schema version declared in the document

members.preview: --check lists waivers whose target identity changes
members.witness: the waiver's declared recipe version and its anchor set
members.hazard: A waiver whose target identity changes is a waiver that silently stops waiving. It must be reported per-waiver, never summarised.

members.preview: --check prints old/new semantics, verifier artifact identities and the new RunId without writing
members.witness: the source RunId plus exact old/new PredicateSemanticsRef, PolicySemanticsRef and verifierArtifactRef values
members.rule: Migration creates a new Run with sourceRunId lineage. It never edits the source Run or reuses its identity.

members.why: A1-VER-06 added runManifestSchema to the identity list. Evidence bundles are reachable from a retained Run and are therefore USER-CUSTODY by V7, but no migrator is specified and the EVIDENCE contract's own custody transition is still unreviewed. Declared as a gap rather than discharged.

migrators.rule: A USER-CUSTODY member with no SPECIFIED migrator may not undergo a breaking change, whatever the version number says.

detectorSemanticDelta.why: B-CSG-04 / CS-04. Exact artifact identity detects that a baseline comparison changed; it CANNOT say whether the change is new code, a changed detector, or the user adopting a new level. All three look like net-new findings, and treating a detector improvement as a regression is how a guardrail loses its users.
detectorSemanticDelta.theProblem: A two-way diff compares (code0, detector0) against (code1, detector1) and attributes the whole difference to code. Two variables moved; one difference was measured.

theFix.name: three-way comparison with a detector pivot
theFix.pivot: Run detector0 over code1. Call the result P.

decomposition.meaning: the same detector, applied to new code, finds something new. This is a real regression.
the detector changed its mind about unchanged code. Not a regression.
the same detector no longer fires — genuine improvement.

theFix.requires: detector0 must still be RUNNABLE. That is exactly what the dual-emit window in the custody policy provides, which is the real reason dual-emit exists: not merely to soften churn, but to make this classification computable at all.

ifPivotUnavailable.rule: The comparison reports which detectors could not be pivoted and why. It NEVER falls back to attributing the whole delta to code.
ifPivotUnavailable.why: Silently attributing a detection delta to the user's code is a false net-new finding presented as a regression — the trust-destroying failure the custody class exists to prevent.

theFix.adoption: A user opting into a new normalisation level or a new rule set is a THIRD case, and it is not inferred: it is an explicit acceptance recorded in the transition, so it never enters the diff as either of the two above.

detectorSemanticDelta.relationToFactIdentity: fact-identity-policy's custody transition protocol supplies the dual-emit window and the many-to-many group mapping this comparison consumes. The two contracts are the same mechanism seen from the baseline side and the identity side.

shipGate.rule: Dual-emit / detector-pivot path MUST NOT ship as the default gate-compare behaviour without either: (a) product acceptance of a documented cost bound (including potential ~2× analysis during multi-major support), or (b) an optimization that keeps pivot off the hot path (cache pivot results; pivot only on detector major change when baseline compare is requested — not on every analysis). Affordability is UNMEASURED; silence is not acceptance (R1-VER-01).
shipGate.defaultUntilDisposition: Pivot runs only when: detector major changes AND a baseline/gate-compare is explicitly requested. Ordinary analysis without compare does not invoke the pivot.
shipGate.forbids: Claiming the pivot is cheap or free; skipping pivot silently and attributing DETECTION-DELTA as CODE-NET-NEW

detectorSemanticDelta.costHonesty: knownLimitations: pivot doubles work during transition. Do not claim affordability without measurement. Correct classification is necessary; unbounded CI cost without disposition makes operators skip pivot and reintroduce false regressions (R1-VER-01).

historicalSemanticsPolicy.selectedStrategy: Retain exact signed native Rust verifier/core payload bytes for every DELIVERY-supported platform, a canonical manifest, detached Ed25519 signature, pinned trust root and raw public key. Historical support is artifact custody, never time based.

scope.rule: Only trusted declarative semantics from the signed offline release enter this path. No public IR or imperative extension promise is created.

historicalSemanticsPolicy.bindingRule: Canonical PredicateSemantics/PolicySemantics bytes are authoritative for verifierArtifactRef, verifierManifestRef, verifierAbi, irFamily, irMajor and trustProfileId. Every field must equal the selected binding and signed manifest. Adjacent metadata never overrides semantics bytes.

releaseCustody.providerModel: bundled-pinned-rustc-driver-sidecar plus signed native Rust verifier/core payload
releaseCustody.executionClaim: NONE; fixture bytes are never executed by this checker

historicalSemanticsPolicy.majorRule: Every IR major has a distinct signed per-platform native payload map and distinct payload identities. A newer host never reinterprets old semantics with its default verifier.
historicalSemanticsPolicy.runImmutabilityRule: Historical verification never mutates the sealed Run. Migration creates a new Run with sourceRunId lineage and never rewrites the source identity.

capabilityJoin.dependencyDirection: evaluation-proof.v5 -> retention-tiers.v10 -> versioning-policy.v5; this join has no downstream dependency
capabilityJoin.dependencyProjection: VERSIONING returns the exact selected semantics, manifest, native payload, detached signature, trust root and raw public-key refs as typed raw-CAS dependencies, each with minimum verifiable capability and typed availability/refusal.
capabilityJoin.exactSetRule: Map the six EP5 historical roles to the v4 fixture kinds below, require exact ref and minimum-capability equality, and require all six rows exactly once. RT10 proofRefs must contain the same six typed raw keys. No alias, omission, duplicate, unreachable edge, weakening, or strengthening is valid.
capabilityJoin.forbidden: Do not copy capability ranks, create a second lattice or demotion state machine, mutate sealedCapability, use TOFU/network lookup, accept descriptor/signature presence as payload custody, or include current availability/effectiveCapability in immutable semantics.
capabilityJoin.authoritativeRead: Unavailable or incompatible custody refuses through existing D9 vocabulary. VERSIONING adds no D9 code, and read-time availability never changes a sealed Run.

supportPosture.basis: artifact custody plus exact compatible offline native payload
supportPosture.rule: No date/count/SLA. Support exists only while the exact selected six-object dependency set is retained and compatible.

trustModel.testKeyUse: RFC8032 deterministic conformance fixture only; not a production release key

cryptographicVerification.mechanism: self-contained RFC8032 Ed25519 verifier in check-versioning.py

agentProtocolNote.position: The agent protocol surface is CONSUMER-CUSTODY for shape, but its negotiation is SESSION-SCOPED: a client advertises the major it wants at connect and is refused if unsupported.
agentProtocolNote.consequence: No multi-release dual-serve obligation is incurred for agents alone. A durable agent runtime that outlives a session would change this, and none exists.
agentProtocolNote.why: Dual-serving every major for a surface whose consumers reconnect every session is cost with no beneficiary.

comparisonFixtures.why: attributing a possible detection delta to the user's code is a false net-new finding presented as a regression

resolves.A1-VER-01: RESOLVED — four USER-CUSTODY migrators specified with migratorId, preview surface, idempotence and witness. Run-manifest is declared NOT-YET-ENFORCEABLE and excluded from the legacy test-reference lists, so VT-02's specification is no longer vacuous. This is not demonstration evidence.
resolves.A1-VER-02: RESOLVED — migrators ship in-release and fetch nothing; a transition needing absent data is a RE-ANALYSIS, reported as such, not a disguised upgrade.
resolves.A1-VER-03: RESOLVED — V9 makes reachability change a versioning review event, and VT-11 checks the evidence reachability graph never points at INTERNAL paths.
resolves.A1-VER-04: RESOLVED — agent protocol negotiation is session-scoped; no multi-release dual-serve obligation without a durable agent runtime.
resolves.A1-VER-05: RESOLVED BY MARKING, NOT BY FIXING — every window carries evidenceGrade GUESSED, the seal rule forbids sealing on a guess, and the corresponding property is NOT DISCHARGED. VT-12 may be permanently unimplementable because the grounding telemetry is what the threat model refuses to collect.
resolves.A1-VER-06: RESOLVED — runManifestSchema added to versionedIdentities as USER-CUSTODY via V7.
resolves.B-SCV2-06: RESOLVED — the D9 citation retargets to the live v1.6 artifact and the dependency DIRECTION is declared: VERSIONING depends on D9, not the reverse.
resolves.B-CSG-04 / CS-04: RESOLVED — the three-way detector-pivot comparison classifies every difference as CODE-NET-NEW, DETECTION-DELTA or CODE-FIXED, with INDETERMINATE when the pivot detector is unavailable. This is also the real justification for the dual-emit window.
resolves.R10-EVD-07 / EVD-PATCH-04: CANDIDATE REPAIR IN V4 — closes R12-EVD-01 with exact semantics equality, signed per-platform native Rust payload custody, retained trust-root/public-key bytes and real Ed25519 verification. Independent rereview remains required; Evidence v3 still points to VERSIONING v3 and is not repaired by this artifact alone.

comparisonSchema.why: The classification results and the migrator declaration were referenced throughout and never typed. Two implementations could emit different vocabularies and both claim conformance — the same defect B-FI-09 raised against the normalisation ladder.

classification.rule: Closed. An unknown classification is rejected, not passed through as advisory.

indeterminateReason.rule: REQUIRED when classification is INDETERMINATE. An unexplained indeterminate is indistinguishable from a bug.

MigratorDeclaration.rule: A migrator with status SPECIFIED and any missing field is a release-gate failure, not a warning.

comparisonSchema.gateRule: Only CODE-NET-NEW may fail a ratchet gate. DETECTION-DELTA and INDETERMINATE are reported and never gate, because neither is evidence the user regressed.

adjudicationRevision.note: Pivot cost ship-gate; support windows consumer-facing evidenceGrade; run-manifest backlog.

implementationBacklog.note: R1-VER-03: USER-CUSTODY evidence bundles without migrator get typed refusal only under V3 — correct, operationally painful. Track when EVIDENCE seals.

role: A-prime v4 cold stored-read reconstruction versioning rejoin

successorRevision.custodyRule: All historical and admitted-authority dependencies join by typed RawCasRef key and exact role. Semantic commitments cannot be physical keys; snapshot body refs remain replayable.
successorRevision.storeAuthorityRule: ProjectStoreAuthority/store-instance/transaction tokens are operational-only, nonserializable and excluded from all historical/current semantic and raw custody identities.

identityStability.reason: Only cold stored-read reconstruction/port continuity changed.

successorRevision.forbiddenBackEdge: No Evidence artifact, checker, digest, RunId, TerminalRunV1, RunAuthorityIndexV1, ProjectStoreAuthority token or store transaction token enters VERSIONING-v8 authority/custody.

coldStoredReadRejoin.rule: A newly opened ProjectStoreAuthority port may reconstruct admitted authority only from its ProjectId-scoped immutable CAS rows plus EvaluationAuthorityIndexV1, then rerun exact admission. Caller candidate, inventory assertion and warm cache are not authority.
coldStoredReadRejoin.identityRule: Index rows, traversal order/state, cache/inventory state and store/transaction tokens are operational-only and excluded from every semantic commitment, raw custody identity and versioned identity.
coldStoredReadRejoin.productionRestartClaim: NONE; checker-only in-memory cold-open reconstruction is not a production restart, durable store, transaction, recovery or atomicity demonstration.

successorRevision.dependencyLabelRule: Current successor inputs are exactly evaluation-proof.v8.json and retention-tiers.v13.json. Older EP/RT labels in byte-preserved predecessor sections are historical lineage only.
